Burn surface-area assessment: 5

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A patient has both blistered partial-thickness burns and surrounding uncomplicated superficial redness. Which rule should be applied to the superficial component when calculating the area used for major-burn severity and resuscitation assessment?

  1. Exclude purely superficial burns from resuscitation TBSA
  2. Include partial- and full-thickness areas in TBSA
  3. Cool the burn safely and assess severity
  4. Re-epithelialization from preserved viable epidermal sources
  5. Inflammatory vasodilation
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Exclude purely superficial burns from resuscitation TBSA

Burn-area estimates used for major burn assessment count partial- and full-thickness injury, not simple superficial erythema.

Understanding the options

Exclude purely superficial burns from resuscitation TBSA
Burn-area estimates used for major burn assessment count partial- and full-thickness injury, not simple superficial erythema.
Include partial- and full-thickness areas in TBSA
Dermal and deeper burns contribute to the burn area used for severity and resuscitation assessment. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
Cool the burn safely and assess severity
Appropriate cool running water first aid and protection are used; ice and additional cold injury should be avoided. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
Re-epithelialization from preserved viable epidermal sources
Superficial injuries retain capacity for epithelial regeneration; deeper loss reduces this reserve. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
Inflammatory vasodilation
Superficial inflammatory hyperemia contributes to the red appearance of a minor burn. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
